title: Effects of agar and pectin on gastric emptying and post-prandial glycaemic profiles in healthy human volunteers
authors: Sanaka M, Yamamoto T, Anjiki H, Nagasawa K, Kuyama Y
journal: Clinical and Experimental Pharmacology and Physiology
population: Healthy male volunteers, Tokyo Metropolitan Komagome Hospital and Teikyo University School of Medicine
funder: Not read: the publisher returned HTTP 403, the archived publisher pages show only the abstract behind a paywall, and the article is absent from PubMed Central. PubMed lists no grant support.
result: From the PubMed abstract: 10 healthy men each received three 450 kcal/500 mL test meals, fibre-free, with 2.0 g agar or with 5.2 g pectin, with a [13C]-acetate breath test and serial blood sampling. Compared with the control meal, the pectin meal prolonged the half 13CO2 excretion time (P < 0.0001) and the time to maximal 13CO2 excretion rate (P = 0.002); neither agar nor pectin affected the post-prandial glucose profile.
